summary: Schema evolution in function-call payloads leads to duplicate tool invocations on multiplexed streaming clients
description:
Issue summary: After a recent behind-the-scenes schema change in how function/tool calls are encoded by the SDKs, a small subset of multiplexed streaming clients experienced duplicate external tool invocations. Impact: Customer reports duplicate downstream side-effects (duplicate job creations and webhook deliveries) for requests that were retried/resumed across SDK versions. Environment: Dedicated cluster in prod (us-west-2), customer uses multiplexed WebSocket streams with mixed clients (python 1.8.x and typescript 2.0.x). Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a multiplexed streaming session from a long-lived Node client (TS 2.0.1) and a Python client (1.8.4) to the same customer session.
2) Send a function/tool call that includes a confirmation ack expectation and an idempotency-derived key (default SDK behavior).
3) While the stream is in flight, trigger a client reconnect from the Python side (simulate flaky network).
4) Observe two downstream tool invocations for the same logical request id in the customer's system within ~15s.
Observed behavior: Two calls to the customer's webhook/service with equivalent payloads but different idempotency baggage values. Logs show the server accepted both as distinct invocations. Expected behavior: Retry/resume/reconnect should not produce duplicate external side-effects when idempotency keys or confirmation tokens identify the request as already-executed.
Additional notes: The customer is on Dedicated and has reserved capacity; traffic spike did not trigger autoscaling-related fallbacks. The duplicates correlate to sessions where client SDK versions were mixed (older Python + newer TS) and where a proxy (edge/ingress) performed a small payload rewrite (normalization of function argument field names).
steps_to_reproduce: Open a multiplexed session with mixed SDK versions (TS + Python)
Send a function call with default idempotency baggage
Induce a client reconnect/resume from one client
Observe duplicate downstream invocations in customer system
logs_and_artifacts: edge-proxy trace: header rewrite applied: func_name->function_name
customer webhook payloads: uuid=job_204, payload checksum matches
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Gomez (Support): Customer reports two job entries created when they expected one. Attached webhook payloads and timestamps.
2026-03-10 10:03 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Requested raw stream logs and request IDs. Asked customer to provide timeframe and sample request_id.
2026-03-10 11:20 - Customer (InstaDoc - DevOps): Provided request_id 6f23b8a2-... and said duplicates happen ~30% of reconnections. Using node-ts 2.0.1 and python-sdk 1.8.4 mixed in same session.

2026-03-10 13:45 - Sofia Martinez (Engineer): Reproduced locally with mixed SDKs. Observed that idempotency key generation differs when function argument key name changes (func_name vs function_name). Edge proxy rewrote field name. This normalized payload makes two distinct idempotency baggage values across versions.

2026-03-11 09:02 - Sofia Martinez: Hypothesis: SDKs derive idempotency baggage from canonicalized payload bytes + sdk-version namespace. A schema rename without cross-version compatibility causes different baggage. Edge proxy rewrite amplifies the mismatch by changing the canonical bytes on transit.
investigation_notes: Confirmed mixed SDK versions produce different canonicalization outputs for identical semantic calls.
Edge proxy normalizer rewrote function argument key from 'func_name' to 'function_name' which changed canonical payload ordering in our serializer.
Idempotency baggage is computed as base64(sha256(namespace||canonical_payload)). Namespace includes SDK version for telemetry; older SDKs used 'sdk:py:1.8.4', newer used 'sdk:ts:2.0.1'.
Reproduced duplicate external webhook delivery in dedicated cluster when reconnect path resumed and server accepted both sequences as new invocations.
No sign of server-side dedup config being incorrectly applied; root cause is key derivation mismatch upstream of dedup check.
impact_summary: Customer-facing side-effects (duplicate job creation and webhook delivery). Affects customers using mixed SDK stacks and edge payload normalizers. Rate: ~20-30% of reconnect/resume events for affected sessions. No platform-wide outage; limited to sessions with mismatched SDK canonicalization and proxy rewrites.
temporary_workaround: Advise customer to: 1) pin SDK versions to a single major for all multiplexed clients in the same session; 2) disable edge payload rewrite for function call fields; OR 3) set explicit idempotency_key in tool call metadata (application-managed) until patch is deployed.
resolution_plan: Engineering will: 1) land a patch to SDKs and server to decouple idempotency baggage namespace from SDK version (PR referenced below), 2) add tolerant canonicalization that ignores harmless key renames when computing dedup keys, and 3) add server-side heuristic that compares payload semantic equality if dedup keys conflict within a short window. Target patch: serving-runtime + SDK hotfix (python 1.8.5, ts 2.0.2).
resolution_notes: In progress - PR opened. QA acceptance pending. After patch, we'll run a canary with the customer's traffic and monitor duplicates for 48h. Customer notified and asked to apply temporary workaround.
next_steps: Merge PRs and release SDK patches (target 2026-03-14)
Coordinate with customer to roll patched SDK to all clients in their sessions
Add alert to detect increases in duplicate webhook deliveries per session
